# SB-1007 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03

## Hazard description
Blasting operations adjacent to Heat Treat hydraulic forging press EQ-P2-L4-HP03 generate respirable and nuisance dust that can migrate into the press enclosure and downstream work areas. Airborne dust presents multiple hazards: operator respiratory exposure, contamination of hydraulic and electronic components, optical sensor fouling, and increased risk of ignition when dust accumulates on hot surfaces or within enclosed housings. The hazard is compounded where housekeeping is inconsistent or where local exhaust capture is inadequate.

Investigation of recent filter loading events and maintenance access delays identified dust ingress into the press cavity and control cabinet plenum during and after adjacent blasting cycles. The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) must be maintained; dust contamination that affects hydraulic valves, fittings, or accumulators risks uncommanded pressure transients that could approach the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), 320 bar, and must be mitigated.

This bulletin addresses control measures to reduce airborne dust migration, protect mechanical and hydraulic components, and reduce operator exposure until permanent engineering solutions are implemented.

## Affected equipment
- EQ-P2-L4-HP03 (Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3) and immediate support equipment including local filtration housings, oil reservoirs, hydraulic manifolds, and press control cabinets.
- Adjacent blasting booths and material handling paths on P2, line P2-L4 that contribute dust loads into the press vicinity.
- Peripheral sensor and actuator housings associated with EQ-P2-L4-HP03 that are susceptible to particulate ingress.

Refer to operating procedures SOP-P2-L4-01, SOP-P2-L4-02, and SOP-P2-L4-03 for standard operating status and baseline maintenance expectations. This bulletin supersedes temporary practices not aligned with those SOPs until formal procedure updates are issued.

## Required controls
Controls are organized in layers: administrative, work-practice, personal protective equipment, and temporary engineering measures. Implement all applicable controls immediately.

Administrative and planning
- Schedule blasting activities to minimize temporal overlap with press cycles for EQ-P2-L4-HP03; coordinate with the press shift supervisor to establish windows when the press is not in operation. Use SOP-P2-L4-01 for coordination protocol.
- Maintain a blasting log that records start and stop times, blasting media used, and location relative to EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Retain logs in the equipment maintenance folder and attach to the maintenance work order for post-blast inspection per SOP-P2-L4-02.

Work-practice and housekeeping
- Before each blasting campaign, perform pre-blast inspection around EQ-P2-L4-HP03 to identify and seal obvious ingress points to the press enclosure and control cabinet with temporary seals or covers.
- After blasting, perform a wet-wipe or HEPA-vacuum cleaning of exposed surfaces on and around EQ-P2-L4-HP03 prior to press startup. Document completion on the press pre-start checklist and file with the operator shift log.
- Prohibit compressed air blow-down for cleaning in areas adjacent to EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Use approved vacuum or wet methods to remove dust.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
- Operators and maintenance personnel performing clean-up or ingress inspection near blasting activities must use respiratory protection as required by the site respiratory protection program and the exposure assessment in SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Use gloves and eye protection suitable for handling contaminated components during clean-up operations. Discard or launder contaminated PPE according to facility procedures.

Temporary engineering measures
- Install temporary localized capture barriers and directional air curtains between blasting sources and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 during blasting cycles. Ensure negative pressure is maintained in the blasting booth to minimize migration.
- Fit temporary pre-filters or protective covers to intake grills and control cabinet vents for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 during adjacent blasting. These covers must be removed and inspected prior to press operation and recorded on the pre-start checklist.
- Where dust accumulation on hydraulic fittings or sensors is observed, perform a documented inspection and cleaning before returning EQ-P2-L4-HP03 to service to ensure no particulate interference with pressure control components.

Monitoring and verification
- Conduct visual inspections of key components on EQ-P2-L4-HP03 after every nearby blasting event and before press start-up. Record findings on the post-blast inspection form and attach to the equipment maintenance record.
- If particulate ingress is confirmed in hydraulic housings, implement the isolation and contamination control steps in SOP-P2-L4-02 and escalate to maintenance engineering for possible oil sampling and filter change per that procedure.
- Track recurring incidents of dust ingress and submit a Contamination Incident Report to maintenance engineering for permanent mitigation design.

Rationale and examples
- Rationale: Dust ingress can accelerate wear on valve spools and seals, contaminate hydraulic oil, and foul sensors, any of which can degrade control fidelity and lead to pressure excursions approaching the system pressure limit. Reducing particulate load decreases unplanned downtime and lowers the risk of hydraulic anomalies at or near the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), 320 bar.
- Example: A post-blast inspection identified abrasive dust on an external pressure transducer housing. After vacuuming and covering the intake vent during subsequent blasts, transducer performance returned to normal and a follow-up oil sample showed no particulate ingress.
- Example: Scheduling blasting during a defined maintenance window allowed the press to be powered down and sealed; clean-up was performed before restart and no contamination-related faults occurred.

Records to keep
- Blasting log for each event (location, media, start/stop) — attach to maintenance work order and retain per facility records policy.
- Post-blast inspection form for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 — include checklist items for filters, vents, hydraulic fittings, and sensors; retain in equipment file.
- Pre-start checklist entries indicating removal of temporary vent covers and completion of cleaning prior to press operation.
- Contamination Incident Reports and any follow-up oil analysis or component replacements referenced to EQ-P2-L4-HP03.

Non-compliance and escalation
- Operators must not start EQ-P2-L4-HP03 if post-blast inspection items are incomplete. If contamination of hydraulic components is suspected, tag out and notify maintenance engineering. Refer to SOP-P2-L4-02 for isolation and contamination control steps.

Related documents
- SOP-P2-L4-01
- SOP-P2-L4-02
- SOP-P2-L4-03

## Effective date
Effective upon issuance of this revision (Rev B). Implement required controls immediately and document compliance as described above.
